title: Sustain & Release
concept:
The last two ADSR stages control the held and ending portions of a note.

Sustain is the level (not a time) at which the envelope holds while the key is pressed. Unlike Attack and Decay, it does not count down — it just waits. A sustain of 1.0 means the note stays at full volume throughout. A sustain of 0.0 means the note silences after the Decay stage, creating a plucked or percussive feel even while the key is held.

Release is the time for the note to fade to silence after the key is released. A very short release (near 0 s) cuts the note off abruptly — useful for staccato playing. A long release (1–3 s) leaves a trailing echo-like tail, like the sustain pedal on a piano or the natural reverb of a room.

The patch has a short release right now. Set the Release to 2 seconds and listen to how the note lingers after you let go of the key.

task.instruction: Set the ADSR's Release to 2 s. Raise the Release knob on the ADSR Envelope, press a key briefly, then release it — hear the note fade out slowly.
